entities.title: A watcher error does not trigger a full reconcile
entities.summary: When a change source asks for a rescan (FileSystemWatcher error, FSEvents must-scan flags), the index only applies the events already queued.
entities.expected: A full reconcile runs when the watcher reports an error or events were dropped, as the README's How it works section said ("a full reconcile runs on .gitignore/HEAD changes, watcher errors and every 5 minutes").
entities.observed: RootIndex.Start subscribes NeedsFullScan to the debounce timer, which calls Drain; Drain reconciles only when the queued paths include a .gitignore, .git/HEAD, .git/info/exclude or a new directory. Changes the watcher dropped stay invisible until the five-minute periodic reconcile, or until a query's barrier re-checks the file.
acceptanceCriteria: Raising NeedsFullScan with an empty queue leads to a Reconcile, and a test covers it.

origin.description: Found while documenting the folder, by reading RootIndex.Start and RootIndex.Drain against the README; not reproduced.

entities.title: The watcher does not catch a rewrite that keeps the stat key
entities.summary: The README's Known limits say a rewrite keeping size, mtime and birth time is caught by the watcher; the code skips it on a watcher event too.
entities.expected: A change event for a known file re-reads it, so a rewrite that keeps size, modification time and birth time gets its new analysis (README, Known limits: "caught by the watcher but not by a restart reconcile").
entities.observed: Drain calls RootIndex.Analyze for a known path, and Analyze returns without reading the file when FileEntry.Matches holds, exactly as a reconcile does.
acceptanceCriteria: Either a watcher event for a known file re-hashes it regardless of the stat key, with a test, or the README's Known limits no longer say the watcher catches it.
